topic: Java equals and hashCode contracts for value objects
tomorrowTopic: How Spring constructor injection resolves dependencies

hook.headline: Equal objects must agree on their hash code
hook.hook: Java equality is not just an equals method decision: hash-based collections also rely on a compatible hashCode implementation.
hook.visualCaption: Equality defines semantic sameness; hashCode provides a compatible bucket hint for hash-based collections.
hook.microExample: same value → equals true → same hash code

mentalModel.title: One equality relation, two methods
mentalModel.coreIdea: equals defines whether two objects are semantically equal. hashCode supports hash-based lookup. The key contract is one-way: objects that are equal must produce the same hash code, while unequal objects may still collide.
mentalModel.keyOutcome: A broken contract can make logically equal keys behave inconsistently in HashMap or HashSet.

code.title: Keep equality and hashing aligned
code.intro: Base both methods on the same fields that define the value object's semantic identity.
code.highlightReason: hashCode uses the same value-defining fields as equals, preserving the required relationship for equal Money instances.
code.takeaway: If equality changes when a field changes, hashing should reflect the same equality definition.
code.professionalNote: For immutable value types, stable equality fields also avoid key mutation problems after insertion into hash collections.

production.title: Why broken equality becomes a real bug
production.scenario: A service constructs two Money instances representing the same value, but one is used as a HashMap key and later lookup with the other unexpectedly misses.
problems: equals says the keys are equal, but inconsistent hash codes can direct lookup to different buckets.
Mutating equality-relevant fields after insertion can also make a key difficult to find using its new state.
production.professionalApproach: Define semantic identity deliberately, use the same fields in equals and hashCode, prefer immutable value objects, and test equality behavior including hash-based collection lookup.
production.debugClue: Two keys print identical business values and equals returns true, yet HashMap.get with the second key returns null.

interview.question: What contract must equals and hashCode satisfy, and why does it matter for HashMap keys?
interview.answer: If two objects are equal according to equals, they must return the same hash code. The reverse is not required because collisions are valid. HashMap uses the hash to narrow candidate entries and then equality to identify a matching key, so inconsistent implementations can make logically equal keys fail lookup.
